RICHARD CHALLENOR---John Stow and Paddy Breslin are fine prospects who have fared particularly well this season. Paddy won the school 440 in a modest 60.5, but in finishing second in the 880 he recorded a personal best 2:09 repeating John Stow's position of last year.
Mick Marshall clocked 11.5 in his heat of the 100 metres and Pat Breslin and Eddie McNally recorded 3:11 and 3:20 in the 1,000 metres s'chase.
Paddy Breslin, also a member of the Richard Challoner team, helped bring them into 3rd team place with 12:28. John Cambridge was 4th in a schools Cross-Country race over 2½ miles at Ewell recently.
Paddy Breslin continued his improvement in the steeplechase with a useful fifth place in the 2,000 metres event. All in all, a very good day for our youngsters.

In the 3,000 metres walk, Wesch, Coates and Lawton made a clean sweep of the medals, following the example of Paddy Breslin and Eddie McNally who, three week's earlier, took the first two places in the Junior steeplechase.
:(Ron Linstead) Paddy Breslin seizes his opportunity to produce the currently fashionable victor's salute as he wins the Surrey County Junior 2,000 metres steeplchase in a comfortable 6:45.8.

John doesn't hold a peak for long, so we must build him up for just the Southern and National events - he may then spring a great surprise! Pat Breslin still lags a little behind the "Big Four", but is improving fast. Slowly, but surely, he is eating into that tantalising gap.
Tony Binda came 50th, John Stow 175th and Pat Breslin 197th The whole team except Mark appeared jaded - Bill although physically below par lacked nothing in determination - to beat Peter.
It was good to see Paddy Breslin back in action in the junior events, and to see John Stow back in winning form, while there was a promising junior steeplechase from Mark Clancy.
Paddy Breslin made a good job of deputising for our star steeplechasers. Paddy did not have a good winter, but with a run free of injury, he could soon be under 10m. in this event.
Mark Clancy maintained his recent improvement to finish 5th and in 8th place was Pat Breslin free for once from the heartbreaking series of injuries which have made his winter season so miserable.
His effort was a courageous one and will be long remembered by those present. Running for an incomplete 'B' team Mark Clancey and Pat.
